geography: Archer City, Mount Barry, Briar Creek, Rattlesnake Canyon and Craddock bonebed
Texas and New Mexico, United States
overview: Named Early Permian Dimetrodon and cf. Dimetrodon teeth document diverse carina and cusp anatomy in a sphenacodontid matrix; neither the sample nor its topology identifies a direct mammalian ancestor.

ecology.diet: Predatory feeding inferred from sphenacodontid tooth anatomy; individual prey is not preserved
ecology.habitat: Fully terrestrial apex-predator interpretation for the sampled sphenacodontids; habitat breadth is unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Not measured by the dental sample
ecology.bodySize: The profile does not infer a genus-wide mass or body-length range
ecology.guild: Terrestrial predator inference bounded to the source's sampled ecological interpretation

traits: MCZ 2779 snout with enlarged anterior maxillary tooth
MCZ 2028 and UMMP 9722 dentary teeth with lingual cusp variation
Carina and denticle character changes optimized in the sampled phylogeny
evidenceSummary: Figures 1–4 and the methods tie named teeth to Early Permian Texas and New Mexico localities; tooth form supports a bounded ecological interpretation, while species attribution of isolated material, performance and ancestry remain unresolved.

commonNameZh: 达善沟基干兽孔类标本
overview: Holotype IVPP V15424 is a fragmentary Middle Permian snout tested in a 71-character morphology matrix; its basal-therapsid position is an analytical result, not direct ancestry.

ecology.diet: Carnivorous diet inferred from cranial and dental morphology
ecology.habitat: Continental Xidagou depositional setting; exact life habitat unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Not preserved by the partial snout
ecology.bodySize: Known from an approximately 100 mm partial snout
ecology.guild: Small terrestrial predator inferred from dentition

traits: Partial snout with cranial and dental character combination
Double canine condition discussed in the diagnosis
Matrix-defined sister position to sampled therapsids
evidenceSummary: The named holotype and published matrix support a bounded basal-therapsid test, while the formation lacks a reliable direct radiometric date and the fossil is not treated as an ancestor.

overview: CT scans and occlusal reconstruction of named Haramiyavia jaws document a Late Triassic haramiyidan whose placement outside crown Mammalia is specific to the cited character matrix.

ecology.diet: Plant processing inferred from complex teeth and wear facets
ecology.locomotion: Not preserved by the profiled jaw material
ecology.bodySize: Small mammaliaform; profile does not infer whole-body mass
ecology.guild: Small terrestrial plant processor inferred from dentition

traits: Reconstructed palinal jaw movement from wear geometry
evidenceSummary: MCZ7/95A–B and MCZ10/G95 support jaw, tooth-wear and matrix claims; auditory ossicles are not preserved in articulation and the matrix result is not a universal crown-boundary statement.

commonNameZh: 摩尔根兽类颅骨标本组
overview: Morganucodon watsoni from Wales and M. oehleri from China anchor a Lower Jurassic skull comparison with both a squamosal–dentary contact and retained articular–quadrate joint; the anatomy is not a linear transition or direct ancestry claim.

ecology.diet: Tooth classes are functionally differentiated, but direct diet is not observed
ecology.habitat: Lower Jurassic source context; life habitat is unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Not established by the skull study
ecology.bodySize: M. watsoni skull is reported as 26 mm long; no order-wide body-size envelope is inferred
ecology.guild: A whole-order ecological guild is not assigned

traits: 26 mm M. watsoni skull and slightly larger M. oehleri skull
Differentiated incisors, canines, premolars and molars
Squamosal–dentary contact with retained articular–quadrate joint
evidenceSummary: Kermack, Mussett and Rigney's pages 1–158 directly describe the two named Lower Jurassic skull samples; the profile keeps locality, taxonomic scope, diet, functional interpretation and crown placement separate.

overview: Near-complete holotype IVPP V16051 preserves a detached ectotympanic and malleus linked to the dentary by ossified Meckel’s cartilage, documenting one anatomical mosaic rather than a universal transition stage.

ecology.diet: Animal-feeding diet inferred from eutriconodont dentition
ecology.habitat: Jiufotang lacustrine depositional setting; exact life habitat unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Terrestrial locomotion inferred; performance not measured
ecology.bodySize: Small-bodied mammal known from a near-complete skeleton
ecology.guild: Small terrestrial faunivore inferred from dentition

traits: Ossified Meckel’s cartilage linking ear and dentary
evidenceSummary: The holotype directly supports the anatomical observations, but the stabilizing function of the ossified cartilage and its evolutionary significance remain interpretations rather than observed performance or ancestry.
